planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall as rains return, in loose, gravelly, humus-rich soil over shaded rock or slope; this fern naturally follows a winter-wet, summer-dry cycle and establishes best when planted at the start of its active growing season.

directions: Plant in deep to partial shade in loose, freely draining, gravelly or humus-rich soil, ideally on a sloped bank or among rock crevices that mimic its native oak-woodland habitat under coast live oaks and bay laurel. Water regularly through the cool, wet season to keep the soil evenly moist; the delicate, pendant fronds on wiry black-brown stems will naturally go dormant and look dead through the dry California summer unless irrigation continues, then re-emerge with fall rains. Avoid heavy, poorly drained soils and hot afternoon sun, both of which quickly scorch or rot the fine foliage. This California native is well suited to shaded woodland gardens, north-facing banks, and container culture where its drought-deciduous habit can be anticipated rather than mistaken for plant loss.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring into humus-rich, well-drained soil tucked among rocks or logs in part sun to light shade; this small creeping fern spreads slowly by rhizomes and is best started close together for quicker groundcover effect.

directions: Plant in part sun to light shade in average, rich, well-drained soil, tucking divisions into rock crevices or among fallen logs to mimic the sheltered limestone sinkholes and hammock edges of its native range. New fronds emerge a distinctive rosy to salmon-pink and mature to a glossy medium green, giving established clumps an attractive two-toned, dwarf Christmas-fern appearance. Water evenly during establishment; once settled, this small, drought-tolerant and deer-resistant fern spreads slowly, interweaving its rhizomes to form a tidy, low groundcover. Excellent for shaded rock gardens, container plantings, fairy gardens, and living walls where a diminutive, textural fern is wanted.
